clue.text: Report of person unpopular in theatre box?

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so we want a word that sounds like the person described

blocks.note: someone who keeps coughing during a play annoys the rest of the audience

explanation.surface: A theatregoer wonders who is being talked about up in one of the private boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: COUGHER and COFFER sound the same. 'Theatre box' looks like one idea, but the definition is just 'box'.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffer is a strongbox or chest for keeping money and valuables.

clue.text: Eg Selkirk players at another team’s ground?

blocks.note: the cast is the actors in a play
a team playing at another team's ground is playing away

explanation.surface: A Scottish team from the town of Selkirk plays an away match.
explanation.walkthrough: Selkirk looks like the Borders town with its rugby club, but it is Alexander Selkirk, the sailor left alone on an island who inspired Robinson Crusoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Selkirk was a real sailor marooned on an island for four years, a famous example of a castaway.

clue.text: Female on Hebridean island, perhaps

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides, off Scotland

explanation.surface: A woman who might live on one of Scotland's western islands.
explanation.walkthrough: F placed on IONA gives the name, and the whole clue describes a Scottish woman who might well be called that, with 'perhaps' marking her as one possible case.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiona is a girl's name of Scottish origin, so a woman from the Hebrides could well be called that.

clue.text: Single European taking top position for a long time

indicators.note: in a down answer the top is the start, so a letter moves up from the bottom to the front

blocks.note: single means one
E for European is the letter that moves, here the last letter of the number

explanation.surface: A European bachelor holds the top job for years.
explanation.walkthrough: The E at the end of ONE climbs to the top of the down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an age, an immensely long stretch of time.

clue.text: I’m against work in progress: shut up about it!

indicators.note: one thing set about another wraps around it, so the 'it' just mentioned goes inside

blocks.note: OP is short for opus, a work
pent means shut up or confined, as in pent-up
something that is on is happening now

explanation.surface: A grumpy worker rejects a project that has already started and tells everyone to be quiet about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' points back to 'in progress', which is what the shutting up goes around. The definition is what such a person might say: 'I'm against'.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent is someone who opposes a thing, so 'I'm against' is that person's own statement.

clue.text: Heads adopting the Italian exercise regime

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the heads hold the other word inside them

blocks.note: pate is an old word for the head
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: Bosses decide to take up a fitness routine from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads' looks like bosses; here they are the heads on people's shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilates is a system of exercises for strengthening the core and improving posture.

clue.text: Rubbish about chemical company upset Defence Ministry mandarins

definitions.note: plural noun for people; the answer is a collective noun for them

indicators.note: one thing about another wraps around it, so the company name sits inside
in a down answer, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run in the opposite order

blocks.note: offal can mean refuse or waste
ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a British chemical company
MoD is the Ministry of Defence

explanation.surface: Top civil servants at the Ministry of Defence are angered by a waste scandal at a chemical firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mandarins' looks like oranges; here it means powerful senior civil servants.
explanation.definitionFit: Officialdom is the body of officials and bureaucrats collectively, the senior civil servants nicknamed mandarins.

clue.text: Diagram showing height above sea level?

blocks.note: first meaning: an architect's drawing of one face of a building
second meaning: how high a place is, as on a map

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one description, a chart of altitudes; the answer is a drawing in its own right and also the altitude itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect's elevation draws one side of a building, and a place's elevation is its altitude.

clue.text: Very small terrier’s head displaying symptom of scabies

indicators.note: the head of a word is its start, so only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of terrier
scabies makes the skin itch

explanation.surface: A tiny terrier keeps scratching, a sign it has scabies.
explanation.definitionFit: Titchy is informal British for tiny, from the music-hall comedian Little Tich.

clue.text: Gable ornament — last one to be installed

indicators.note: something installed is fitted into place inside, so a letter goes into the other word

blocks.note: final means last
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A builder adds the decoration on top of a roof gable as the last job.
explanation.definitionFit: A finial is a decorative knob or spike fixed at the top of a gable, spire or post.

clue.text: Cost of cutlery for one rarely seen in the UK?

definitions.text: one rarely seen in the UK

blocks.note: a spoon is a piece of cutlery
a bill is what something costs you

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a set of knives and forks is too pricey for anyone in Britain to buy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cost of cutlery' means the cost belonging to the cutlery, so the cutlery comes first and the cost second.
explanation.definitionFit: The spoonbill is a wading bird with a flat spoon-shaped beak, only an occasional visitor to Britain.

clue.text: Fast bowler famously intercepted one once

blocks.note: first meaning: quick, swift on its feet
second meaning: Sir Francis Drake, said to have finished his game of bowls before sailing against the Spanish Armada in 1588

explanation.surface: A cricket story about a quick bowler who once made a famous catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast bowler' looks like cricket, but the bowler plays bowls on a lawn: Drake on Plymouth Hoe. What he went out to stop was the Armada.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet is an old adjective for swift, and a fleet is a group of warships, like the Spanish Armada.

clue.text: Grotesque, concealing entrance — one’s flouting the law

indicators.note: a thing concealing something has it hidden inside it, so the other pieces go within

blocks.note: antic is an old word for grotesque or bizarre
an arch is a curved entrance or gateway
one is I, and 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A grotesque figure hides in a doorway, the sort of person who ignores the law.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the entrance and 'one's' go inside the grotesque word, one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone anarchistic rejects all government and rules, so they ignore the law.

clue.text: Moving outwards, carting fuel about

indicators.note: about means all around and in disorder, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tanker driver heads out of town carrying fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A centrifugal force pushes away from the centre of a spinning object, so it acts outwards.

clue.text: Possibly Yggdrasil’s remains

blocks.note: first meaning: a kind of tree, of which Yggdrasil, the world tree of Norse myth, is one example
second meaning: what is left after something burns

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the remains of a mythical tree. In fact 'Possibly Yggdrasil' is one meaning, an example given with 'possibly', and 'remains' is the other.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse myth Yggdrasil is a huge ash tree, and ash is also the powder left after burning.

clue.text: Stadium beside lake accommodating second team

indicators.note: something accommodating a guest takes it in, so one piece goes inside the others

blocks.note: an arena is a stadium
L is the abbreviation for lake
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A sports ground next to a lake is home to a club's reserve side.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a famous English Premier League football team based in north London.

clue.text: Right people to run a business brilliantly!

blocks.note: star means brilliant, outstanding
a board of directors runs a company

explanation.surface: A cheer for the right management team running a company superbly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brilliantly' comes last in the clue but goes first: a board that performs brilliantly is a STAR BOARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Starboard is the right-hand side of a ship or aircraft, looking forward.

clue.text: Former secret police force’s lack of activity

blocks.note: the Stasi was East Germany's secret police
the apostrophe s is kept as written

explanation.surface: A historical note about how idle the old East German secret police had become.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's turns out to be part of the answer, not just grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of standstill, where nothing moves or changes.

clue.text: Abandon espionage ultimately leaving moles operating

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of the spying word counts
a letter that is leaving goes away, so it is taken out of the next word

blocks.note: the last letter of espionage
a mole is a stone pier or breakwater, so moles are jetties
a machine that is operating is on

explanation.surface: A spymaster tells an agent to give up spying now that the moles in the service are active.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moles' looks like double agents; here it means harbour walls. Take the E out of JETTIES and add ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison something is to throw it away or abandon it, as when cargo is dumped from a ship.

clue.text: Brilliant major’s back in charge of drill, perhaps

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: fab is slang for brilliant
the last letter of major
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: An army major is a brilliant drill instructor, back in command of the parade ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drill' looks like military marching; here it is a cloth, so 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Drill is a strong twilled cotton cloth, used for work clothes, so it is one kind of fabric.

clue.text: Porter secures painter on front of canal boat

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is used
to secure something is to hold it fast inside, so the songwriter's name wraps around the rest

blocks.note: Cole Porter was the American songwriter
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
the first letter of canal

explanation.surface: A dock porter ties up an artist's narrowboat at the start of the canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a dock worker or a drink, but it is the songwriter Cole Porter. The painter sits on the canal's first letter, and both go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A coracle is a small round boat made of wickerwork covered with hide, used in Wales and Ireland.

clue.text: Tonal inflection that may be perfect for musicians

definitions.text: that may be perfect for musicians

blocks.note: first meaning: the rise and fall of the voice in speech

blocks.clueFragment: that may be perfect for musicians
blocks.note: second meaning: a sequence of chords closing a phrase, and a perfect one ends on the home chord

explanation.walkthrough: 'Perfect' sounds like praise; in music theory a perfect cadence is a technical name for the chords V then I.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadence is both the rhythm of speech and the chord progression that closes a musical phrase.

clue.text: Sound European means of transferring funds

indicators.note: sound tells us the word is to be heard, not spelt, so we want its sound-alike

blocks.note: a Czech is a European, a person from the Czech Republic

explanation.surface: A reliable European bank offers a solid way to move money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective, as in a sound European; it is the signal to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque is a written order telling a bank to pay money from your account to someone else.

clue.text: Empty-headed jazz fan in filthy dwelling

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the fan goes within the dwelling

blocks.note: a sty is a pigsty, a byword for a filthy home
cat is old slang for a jazz fan

explanation.surface: A dim-witted jazz lover living in squalor.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatty is British informal for scatterbrained, forgetful and disorganised.

clue.text: Senior officer in front of “Black Swan”

blocks.note: CO is a commanding officer
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A senior officer stands in front of a pub called the Black Swan.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Black Swan' look like a name, a pub or a film, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cob is a male swan; the female is a pen.

clue.text: Blooming thing blacksmiths return to, saving time

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safe inside, so a letter is held within
to return is to go back, so the little word that follows is read backwards

blocks.note: blacksmiths work at a forge, so they are forgemen
T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written

explanation.surface: Blacksmiths go back to work on a flower, managing to save time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' applies only to the little word 'to', not to the blacksmiths.
explanation.definitionFit: The forget-me-not is a small flowering plant with blue blooms, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Born in Paris, first of Dieppe’s unknown poor

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the French port's name

blocks.note: née is French for born
the first letter of Dieppe
in algebra the unknowns are x, y and z

explanation.surface: Someone born in Paris joins the anonymous poor of Dieppe, a French port.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy people lack money and the basics of life; they are poor.

clue.text: Pluck of a couple of Scots, meeting New Guinea’s leaders

indicators.note: leaders go in front, so each of the two place-name words gives its opening letter

blocks.note: twa is Scots for two
the first letters of New and Guinea

explanation.surface: Two brave Scottish explorers meet the chiefs of New Guinea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluck' looks like courage; here it means to pluck a string.
explanation.definitionFit: To twang a string is to pluck it so it makes a sharp ringing sound.

clue.text: Noble setting for Lucullus’s First Legion?

definitions.note: used as an adjective: very many

indicators.note: a setting holds a jewel in place around it, so one letter is mounted inside
first picks out only the opening letter of the Roman general's name

blocks.note: a countess is a noblewoman
the first letter of Lucullus

explanation.surface: Where the noble general Lucullus might have stationed his First Legion in ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Legion' looks like a Roman unit; 'First' goes with Lucullus and 'Legion' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: When we say their number is legion, we mean there are too many of them to count.

clue.text: Naval man giving rise to deserter

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means reading from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a rat is someone who deserts, like a rat leaving a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A sailor turns into a deserter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar, or Jack Tar, is an old slang name for a sailor.

clue.text: Vocalist in America greeting famous countertenor

blocks.note: yo is an informal American hello
Alfred Deller was an English countertenor who revived the voice type

explanation.surface: An American singer says hello to a famous countertenor.
explanation.definitionFit: A yodeller is a singer who switches fast between chest voice and falsetto, as in Alpine songs.

clue.text: Colourful writer’s cape material

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cape on maps
rayon is a synthetic fabric

explanation.surface: A flamboyant author shows off the cloth of their cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colourful writer' looks like a lively author; it is the answer itself, a tool that writes in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayon is a stick of coloured wax used for drawing and writing.
